evals.prompt: I need a docs page for our hardware docs site (Sphinx with MyST markdown) on hooking up the little SSD1306 OLED module to a Pi 4 over I2C. I've dumped everything I know into evals/files/oled-facts.md including which photos we have in photos/. Write the page(s) as markdown files in the output directory. It's for someone at the bench with the module and a Pi in front of them.
evals.expected_output: A how-to page (and possibly a separate troubleshooting reference) with the fixed headings What you need / Steps / Check / If it fails / Next; one imperative step per action with place, action and result; the available photos placed in the steps they belong to (not all at the top); a parts list with quantities; the 5 V warning as text at the step, not a callout carrying a step; no 'Future:', no 'Sources:' section, no lab counts; sources as inline links; scope sentences first; front matter; no banned words.
assertions: The output is a Markdown how-to page whose level-2 headings are exactly 'What you need', 'Steps', 'Check', 'If it fails', 'Next' in that order
Every numbered step contains exactly one imperative action and states the result or what the reader sees
The available photos (oled-front.jpg, oled-header.jpg, pi4-header-corner.jpg, wired.jpg) are referenced in the steps or parts list they belong to, with non-empty alt text, not all grouped at the top
The parts list under 'What you need' gives each part with a quantity, one per line
No page contains the words 'Future', 'Sources:', 'TODO', 'just', 'simply', 'easy', 'currently', 'soon' or the lab module counts (five, eight)
The page opens with one to three sentences stating what it covers, for whom and what it leaves out, and carries front matter with type, owner, reader and review
The 'If it fails' section lists, for the bench faults given, what you see, the likely cause and the fix
Source documents (datasheet, Raspberry Pi documentation, luma.oled README) appear as inline descriptive links in the sentences that need them, not as a sources list

evals.prompt: Our relay HAT page in docs/hardware/relay-hat.md is a mess and people keep getting it wrong at the bench — see evals/files/messy-page.md. Can you rework it into proper documentation? Put the resulting page or pages in the output directory and tell me what you changed and why.
evals.expected_output: The page split by type: an explanation/overview of the HAT, a how-to for fitting and testing it with fixed headings and one step per action, a reference for the GPIO mapping (and the troubleshooting rows), cross-linked; 'Future:' section and 'Where the facts come from' removed with the planned items pointed at issues; sources as inline links; the light/dark double image replaced by one themed figure; counts and 'currently' removed; 'just', 'simply', 'please note', 'in order to' gone; the TODO filed as an issue rather than left; a short list of what changed and why.
assertions: The output contains more than one page, each of a single type (explanation, how-to, reference), and they link to each other
The how-to page has exactly the headings 'What you need', 'Steps', 'Check', 'If it fails', 'Next' and each step is one imperative action with its result
The GPIO mapping (K1 GPIO 26, K2 GPIO 20, K3 GPIO 21, K4 GPIO 19) is presented as a table or generated reference, with header pin numbers, not as prose
No output page contains 'Future:', 'Where the facts come from', 'Sources:', 'TODO', 'coming soon', 'currently', 'just', 'simply', 'please note' or 'in order to'
The planned Pi 5 support and the web page are either removed from the reader pages or confined to a roadmap/plans note that names issue #17 or another issue
The light and dark images are not both offered as separate images to the reader; a single themed figure mechanism or one image is used
The host counts ('five of our Pi 4 hosts', '9 of them in the lab') are removed
The response explains what was changed and why, referring to the reader's needs

evals.prompt: Before I merge it, can you review the fpgacheck docs page in evals/files/fpgacheck-page.md? It's meant to be the how-to for someone with a board on a Pi who wants to check the wiring. Write your review to review.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A review with a use-it pass (one row per step: could I do it from what is on the page, what did I guess, what did I look for and not find), an audit pass marking facts as sourced or not, and a shortcut hunt; findings include: the page mixes how-to with reference (options) and explanation (how detection works); the title is not 'How to…'; 'just', 'easy', 'currently', 'not yet', 'note:' callouts carrying a prerequisite (sudo on Pi 5); step 2 is not an action and buries explanation; step 3 has no result; drifting number (14 tests); 'Next' has six links and none are real links; the apt key line pipes into tee without the keyring path being created and the sources list is never added, so the install cannot work as written; findings as fix-or-file items.
assertions: The review contains a step-by-step use-it pass with one entry per numbered step saying whether the reviewer could do it from the page and what was missing
The review identifies that the page mixes page types (how-to with an options reference and a detection explanation) and recommends splitting
The review flags the title 'Using fpgacheck' as not naming the task in the house form (How to …)
The review flags the banned or rotting words present (just, easy, currently, not yet) and the drifting count of 14 tests
The review flags that the sudo-on-Pi-5 requirement is a prerequisite hidden in a note and must precede the steps
The review flags that the installation commands cannot work as written (no apt sources entry is added; the keyring directory is not created)
The review flags that 'Next' has more than five entries and that they are not links
Findings are presented as fix-or-file items, not as a rewritten page
